candidate_windows.window_text:
Our experiments are implemented in Tensorflow (Abadi et al., 2016) on an NVIDIA Tesla P100 GPU. For our model and all baselines, we follow the same setting as described below. We pad or cut the input to 100, 20, 100 words for dialogue generation, paraphrasing, and storytelling, respectively. The truncation length is decided based on the observation that there is no significant improvement when increasing input length. The minimum decoding step is 5, and the maximum step is 20 for

all tasks. Experiments were performed with a batch size of 256, and we use Adam optimizer (Kingma and Ba, 2015) as our optimizing algorithm. During the test stage, the beam-search size is set to 4 for all methods and the checkpoint with the smallest validation loss is chosen. Note that for better performance, our model is built based on BERT, and the decoding process is the same as Transformer (Vaswani et al., 2017). Finally, due to the limitation of time and memory, small settings are used in the pre-training baselines.
